scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director) requested building an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06)
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed on ACTUAL meter reads, not estimated reads (E-03)
Field manual-read route completion is 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts (E-01)
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to over 1200/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-06), and 59% of those disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed on ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimated reads (E-03) — so the dominant mechanism is billing import incorrectly accepting or processing actual reads into wrong bills, not estimate substitution from field/AMI read shortfalls. Tariff changes (E-02) and slow dispute-response capacity (E-04) are ruled out as drivers of the surge.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: Still shows manual-read route completion at 0.88 against the 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts — a real field-read shortfall. It no longer supports PR-CHAIN-5's framing of the field shortfall as a comparably weighted driver of the 'separate' estimated-dispute branch, since E-12 shows billing-import rejection (1184/1240, 95%) rather than missing field reads (56) dominates that branch.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

H-SLOW-TICKET-RESPONSE.statement: SH-CS frames the dispute surge as a ticket-handling capacity/response problem solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused incorrect acceptance/substitution of reads, producing systematically wrong bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The AMI vendor's nightly MDMS export (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or delivering incomplete/invalid AMI reads since August, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL.statement: MeterWorks field reading routes went incomplete or reads failed to upload since August, increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-SURGE.statement: Independent of which upstream read source failed, the estimate-substitution step itself increased in volume or error rate since August, directly driving wrong bills.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are billed on ACTUAL reads, suggesting a cause distinct from estimate substitution, such as incorrect acceptance or processing of actual reads in billing import, is driving most of the dispute surge.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-VALIDATION.statement: Billing import's high-consumption validation check incorrectly rejects valid, pre-cutoff AMI actual reads that were successfully exported, converting them into wrong/disputed bills.

H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH.statement: Firmware v4.2's register_unit scale (0.1 m3 vs legacy v3.x's m3), rolled out 2026-06, causes billing import's high-consumption check to misread valid actual consumption as 10x higher, triggering REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.question: What specific billing import mechanism (e.g., a validation rule change) causes incorrect acceptance or processing of ACTUAL meter reads into wrong bills?
U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation requires a billing-config rule fix or a different corrective action, and whether any bill-write/credit action under K-BILLWRITE is ever justified.
U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes coinciding with August and cross-reference against disputed ACTUAL-read bills (E-03).
U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: No bill adjustments and no auto-fix agent; continue read-only investigation of billing-config.
U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution: E-12 shows 1184 valid, pre-cutoff AMI actual reads exported to billing were rejected with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, identifying the billing-import high-consumption validation check as the mechanism; a DA-RULES (billing-config) audit is still advisable to confirm rule-change timing and full attribution.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does the field manual-read route completion shortfall (E-01, 0.88 vs 0.95 target) contribute to any portion of the disputed-bill population, given E-12 shows the ESTIMATED-dispute bucket is driven by AMI-channel billing-import rejection (1184/1240) rather than missing manual field reads?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether field dispatch/staffing remediation belongs in the solution scope at all, or is a separate parallel issue.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Query route-log/billing-db to check whether any disputed-bill accounts are on manual-read (non-AMI) routes.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Track field route completion via SC-ROUTE-COMPLETION-TARGET as a separate parallel issue, not yet confirmed as a dispute-surge driver.

U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Once vendor-provisioned MDMS export access is available, would AMI read event data change the attribution of actual-read billing errors (billing-import-side vs AMI-side)?
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Could shift root-cause ownership from ORG-UTIL billing import to ORG-AMI data quality, changing who must remediate.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Vendor (ORG-AMI) provisions MDMS export access; retry the mdms-export read-events query.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Treat H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE as rejected per E-03 until new vendor data arrives.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: With MDMS export access now provisioned (E-11), AMI read event data (E-12) shows the majority of actual-read errors occur billing-import-side (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) rather than AMI-side, since reads were received before cutoff and exported successfully.

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Does a drop in CRM-logged monthly dispute volume (M-DISPUTE-VOL) fully capture 'correct bills' (G-1), or could ticket volume fall without the underlying unit-scaling defect being fixed?
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Determines whether volume alone is a trustworthy success signal or must be paired with the rejection-rate metric.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Track M-REJECTED-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-SHARE and billing-config rule status alongside M-DISPUTE-VOL to confirm the mechanism, not just the symptom, is fixed.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat dispute-volume improvement as necessary but not sufficient evidence of a billing-accuracy fix.

U-ACTUAL-DISPUTE-MECHANISM.question: Does the same billing-import unit-scaling defect (BV-17 + firmware v4.2) also explain some or all of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-03), or do they have a separate cause?
U-ACTUAL-DISPUTE-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether fixing BV-17 alone resolves most of the dispute surge or only the formerly-ESTIMATED subset.
U-ACTUAL-DISPUTE-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Cross-reference billing-db disputed ACTUAL-read bills with mdms-export firmware/register data for the same accounts.
U-ACTUAL-DISPUTE-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Report the ACTUAL-read dispute mechanism as unconfirmed (KNOWN_LIMITATION) until the cross-reference query runs; do not claim the fix resolves ACTUAL disputes yet.

U-RULE-FIX-GOVERNANCE.question: Who has authority to deploy a corrected version of BV-17, and is that change itself subject to any approval process not yet captured in state.constraints?
U-RULE-FIX-GOVERNANCE.decision_impact: Determines whether the solution can only recommend the fix or must also route it through a specific approval path.
U-RULE-FIX-GOVERNANCE.resolution_path: Confirm with SH-BILL/ORG-UTIL the change-management process for billing-config rule deployments.
U-RULE-FIX-GOVERNANCE.safe_placeholder: Deliver the rule fix as a recommendation to Billing Operations (SH-BILL), not an automated action, pending confirmation of their change process.

A-READ-TYPE-SPLIT-MATCHES-SURG.statement: The ACTUAL/ESTIMATED read-type split of disputed bills (E-03) is assumed to apply to the same Aug-Sep surge population measured in E-06, not an unrelated historical sample.

A-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANIS.statement: A billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, CANDIDATE) is assumed to be a plausible proximate cause of the actual-read billing errors, pending an audit of DA-RULES.

A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-ESTIMATED-ON.statement: The field route completion shortfall (E-01) and staffing claim (E-07) are assumed to affect only the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes, not the ACTUAL-read majority.

A-UNIT-SCALING-FIX-SUFFICIENCY.statement: Correcting billing import rule BV-17 to apply unit scaling for firmware v4.2 meters is assumed sufficient to stop REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION misclassification, since no other validation differences are evidenced.

A-SURGE-TIMING-CAUSATION.statement: The dispute surge's August 2026 onset (E-06) is assumed to be caused by BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment (E-14) rather than a coincidental concurrent change, since no other dated Aug-01 billing/AMI change is evidenced.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-06).
1184 of 1240 disputed bills billed as ESTIMATED reads actually originate from valid AMI actual reads rejected at billing import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12).

Field manual-read route completion is 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts (E-01), a parallel issue not yet confirmed as related to the dispute surge.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-06). The dominant confirmed mechanism: billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-14), compares raw register values against 12-month m3 history; for firmware v4.2 meters that record in 0.1 m3 units (rolled out 2026-06, E-13), this misreads valid actual consumption as ~10x higher, triggering REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejection of valid, pre-cutoff, successfully-exported AMI actual reads (E-12). The rejected reads are substituted with estimated billing, accounting for 1184 of the 1240 disputed bills billed as ESTIMATED reads (E-12), producing wrong bills that drive dispute tickets. The mechanism's reach into the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-03) is not yet separately confirmed.

The rejected reads are substituted with estimated billing, accounting for 1184 of the 1240 disputed bills billed as ESTIMATED reads (E-12), producing wrong bills that drive dispute tickets. proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) reported dispute tickets roughly doubling since August and asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix whatever was causing wrong bills (CL-01). Investigation confirmed the volume doubling (E-06: ~600/month Jun-Jul to 1180-1260/month Aug-Sep) and traced the dominant mechanism to billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-14), which misreads firmware v4.2 meters recording in 0.1 m3 units (E-13) as ~10x consumption, rejecting valid actual reads with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12) and forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of 1240 "ESTIMATED" disputed bills (E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17). The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no holds): the agent delivers an audit of the defect, a scoped fix recommendation, route-completion correlation, dispute-trend monitoring, and formal retirement of the original auto-answer/auto-fix request (since tickets are within SLA per E-04 and K-BILLWRITE bars automated bill writes), but it excludes quantifying how much of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-03) share the same defect, because that item is blocked by an open, high-impact verification obligation required before release.
key_points: The dispute surge (E-06) was initially framed around a majority of ACTUAL-read disputed bills (1785/3025, E-03) as a distinct cause (PD-1@v1), but that framing was invalidated when E-12 showed 1184 of the 1240 'ESTIMATED' disputes actually originate from valid AMI actual reads rejected at billing import.

Root cause confirmed: rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-14), misinterprets firmware v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 register units (rolled out 2026-06, E-13) as ~10x consumption, triggering REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections of valid pre-cutoff reads (E-12), corroborated by E-15, E-16, and E-17 (1184 affected accounts).

SH-CS's original request to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills (CL-01) was retired: dispute response times are within SLA (E-04, median 1.6d/p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target), ruling out a response-capacity problem, and K-BILLWRITE prohibits any automated bill-write actions.

Release scope delivered: audit of the unit-scaling defect, correlation of field route completion with estimated disputes, dispute-volume trend monitoring, a scoped BV-17 fix recommendation, and formal retirement of the auto-fix request (all tied to DA-RULES, DA-ROUTE, DA-TICKET, SH-CS).

Excluded from release: quantifying what share of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills share the same unit-scaling defect, because VOB-U-ACTUAL-DISPUTE-MECHANISM (HIGH impact, required before release) remains open.

Tariff change was ruled out as a cause (E-02, E-05, CL-02), and a field-staffing-driven estimate-substitution explanation (E-01, E-07, CL-03) was shown to be secondary once E-12 established the import-rejection mechanism.
limitations_explained: The agent could not determine how much of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-03) are explained by the same BV-17 unit-scaling defect; this analysis is blocked and left out of the release scope.
billing-config is a read-only tool in the tool surface, so this agent cannot deploy or verify deployment of a corrected BV-17 rule itself; any fix must be applied by someone else.
It is unresolved who within ORG-UTIL holds authority to approve and deploy a corrected BV-17 rule, and whether any write-capable billing-config tool exists for that purpose (open unknown/obligation).

The completeness of underlying data (DA-BILL, DA-ROUTE, DA-TICKET) and the delivery/semantic validity of the field-read and AMI-export data handoffs are unknown, adding residual uncertainty to the audit, correlation, and monitoring outputs produced.
A future drop in monthly dispute volume may not by itself confirm the unit-scaling defect was actually fixed, since that metric could fall for other reasons.
